GOVERNOR BRUCE KING
TO THE COMMISSION
LADD S. GORDON
JUL 2 5LOTP TODD, CHAIRMAN CENTRAL
STATE PLANKING EDWARD MUNOZ
WARD MUNOZ
ALBERT J. BLACK
ALBUQUERQUE
ROBERT H. FORREST
CARLSBAD
July 20, 1972
DEPARTMENT OF GAME AND FISH
STATE CAPITOL SANTA FE 87501
Mr. David King, Director State Planning Office Executive Legislative Building Santa Fe, New Mexico 87501
Dear David:
We have reviewed the Draft Environmental Statement prepared by the Bureau of Outdoor Recreation, Department of the Interior, proposing Department implementation of Executive Order 11644, pertaining to use of off-road vehicles on public lands.
The statement is well prepared and adequately presents the impacts on wildlife. We endorse the implementation of Executive Order 11644 as it should be beneficial to wildlife.
The Department of Game and Fish has long been concerned with off-road vehicle travel as it pertains to hunting and fishing and to disturbance of wildlife. Reasons for this concern are reflected on pages 13, 14, 15, and 16 in the statement under the discussion of Physical and Biologic Impacts.
We are in concurrence with you that guidelines for off-road vehicles as proposed by the Bureau of Outdoor Recreation for federal lands could be applied to our state lands and we would welcome the opportunity to participate in a meeting to discuss this.
For your information actions that we have taken concerning off-road vehicle travel is presented below:
